children: SEDEMAC investors A91 Partners, Xponentia, NJRN Family Trust and Mace offload shares worth Rs 1,456 crore after IPO lock-in expiry

SEDEMAC institutional investors A91 Partners, Xponentia, NJRN Family Trust and Mace Private Limited have collectively offloaded shares worth Rs 1,456.38 crore through multiple bulk deals, shortly after the IPO lock-in period expired, as per a media report
A91 Partners, through its holding entity A91 Emerging Fund II LLP, sold 16.10 lakh SEDEMAC shares at an average price of Rs 3,010 apiece, raising Rs 484.9 crore

Xponentia sold 16.85 lakh shares across three bulk deals for Rs 507.4 crore, while Mace Private Limited sold 7.28 lakh shares worth Rs 219 crore. NJRN Family Trust offloaded 4.5 lakh shares for around Rs 135 crore
HDFC Life Insurance sold 3.63 lakh shares while acquiring 4.02 lakh shares during the transactions

The shares were bought by institutional investors including the Government of Singapore, Amansa Holdings, Invesco Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, Monetary Authority of Singapore and T Rowe Price International Discovery Fund

The Government of Singapore acquired 10.23 lakh shares, followed by Amansa Holdings with 4.63 lakh shares, SBI Mutual Fund with 5.25 lakh shares and Invesco Mutual Fund with 3.54 lakh shares. The Monetary Authority of Singapore and T Rowe Price International Discovery Fund acquired 2.37 lakh and 2.32 lakh shares, respectively
This is the second instance in which these investors have reduced their holdings in SEDEMAC after selling shares through the company's IPO earlier this year
The IPO comprised entirely an offer-for-sale component, through which SEDEMAC investors sold 80.43 lakh shares and raised a cumulative Rs 1,087 crore
Xponentia Capital Partners, Mace, IIT-Bombay's SINE, 360 ONE and HDFC Life Insurance were among the selling shareholders in the IPO

SEDEMAC was founded in 2007 by IIT-B professor Shashikanth Suryanarayana and his students Pushkaraj Panse, Manish Sharma and Amit Dixit. The company designs and manufactures electronic control systems for mobility and industrial applications, with its mobility segment contributing nearly 86 per cent of revenue
SEDEMAC Mechatronics reported a 95.1 per cent year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 33.3 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 17.1 crore in the year-ago quarter
Operating revenue rose 42.5 per cent to Rs 309.8 crore from Rs 217.4 crore
